newsitem.title: GREECE: Danger warning for Britons after Corfu killing.
newsitem.headline: Danger warning for Britons after Corfu killing.

text.p: Britain's embassy in Athens warned its citizens on Friday about dangerous boat thieves on the Greek holiday island of Corfu after a tourist was shot dead, apparently by a raiding party from neighbouring Albania.

A travel advisory obtained from the embassy warns British tourists visiting Corfu by boat to stay in harbours where their craft can be guarded and says visitors should avoid marinas from midnight to 6 a.m.
British tourist Keith Hedley, 57, from Kent was shot dead on Thursday when he tried to stop thieves from stealing a power dinghy tied to his yacht in the early hours of the morning.

Police said armed boat thieves operating by speedboat from the nearby Albanian coast were suspected of killing Hedley. They said the gunmen headed straight for Albania, eight kms (4.8 miles) away, after the incident.
The travel advisory said: "This incident, following on from an earlier incident in June when shots were fired at a tourist hotel, comfirms the continuing threat posed by boat thieves."
The Foreign Office issued a warning to British holidaymakers three months ago after boat thieves opened fire with automatic weapons on a coastal holiday resort on Corfu.
Hedley was docked at Gouvia marina, near the main town of Corfu. He was asleep with three friends on the yacht when he heard the thieves and interrupted them, police said.
